I will keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou, the safest way for me to farm is still the wheat-maize rotation. I know this system, the machines fit it, the buyers are easy to find, and it spreads my risk across the year. I do not want to gamble on crops that need more skill, more labor, or a less certain market. So I will keep all my land in winter wheat first, then follow with summer maize after the wheat harvest.

I will manage wheat with moderate fertilizer, not too much nitrogen, because too much pushes soft growth and raises lodging and disease risk. I will plough before wheat to turn the soil and help store moisture, then irrigate a few key times if water allows: after sowing, at jointing, and around grain filling. I will spray only when needed, mainly for weeds and common diseases or insects. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize with hybrid seed, because hybrid maize gives me more stable yield. For maize, I will use rotary tillage to save time and catch the season, put fertilizer in a balanced way, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use limited but practical. My goal is not the highest possible yield on paper; my goal is a stable harvest, controlled cost, and work I can manage myself.
